benchmark_source: artifacts/v2/phase3_benchmark_manifest.json (benchmark_version per manifest; development+validation splits only, phase3_heldout NOT touched)
candidate: Candidate C - ResearchQuery-driven hybrid (orchestration/source_selection.py + orchestration/query_compilers.py + orchestration/registry.py, real execution)
caveats_added_on_independent_review: Source-routing F1/exact-match (1.0) is not apples-to-apples with Candidate A's (0.759/0.576): select_sources() here reads requested_evidence_types directly from each benchmark case's hand-authored ResearchQuery-shaped input, which was written consistent with that case's own gold_required_sources. Candidate A was scored from raw original_query text through a real, imperfect planning LLM. This run's 1.0 shows the deterministic mapping logic correctly implements its own contract; it does not show equivalent routing quality against a real, noisy Phase-2 NLU extraction. Do not cite '1.0 vs 0.759' as a direct routing-quality improvement without this qualifier. See docs/v2/PHASE3_CANDIDATE_C_MEASUREMENT.md Section 0.

No PubMed query-content/concept-coverage metric was computed against gold_query_must_contain_concepts, despite the benchmark providing it for this purpose. Spot check (case PM-001) found the compiled query missing 2 of 4 required gold concepts. Not reflected in any metric below. See docs/v2/PHASE3_CANDIDATE_C_MEASUREMENT.md Section 0.

tool_selection.valid_registered_tool_rate_note: By construction 1.0 for every call that reaches `calls` in per-case results: orchestration/registry.py's ToolRegistry.validate_call() is a hard boundary every compiled ToolCall must pass before being counted as a real call at all. Calls that failed registry lookup are recorded separately in registry_errors, not silently dropped from this rate's numerator.
tool_selection.get_drug_info_reachability_note: Unlike Candidate A (structurally unreachable - agent/nodes.py has no dispatch branch for get_drug_info at all), Candidate C's ChEMBL compiler (orchestration/query_compilers.py compile_chembl_call) selects get_drug_info whenever an entity carries a ChEMBL-normalized canonical_id - CH-013, CH-014, MS-009, MS-012 are all reachable and correctly routed here.

parameter_quality.schema_valid_rate_note: 1.0 by construction for every call counted here - ToolCall subclasses (orchestration/models.py) validate their own arguments at pydantic-construction time inside the compiler, and DEFAULT_REGISTRY.validate_call() re-checks registry+schema before a call is ever added to `calls`. A compiler that would have produced an invalid value (FL-001 status, FL-002 phase) instead OMITS that field per query_compilers.py's documented rule, so schema_valid_rate=100% is a structural guarantee here, not a measured coincidence - this directly satisfies PHASE3_GATE_PLAN.md Section 4 gate 3.
parameter_quality.pubmed_concept_coverage_note: Deterministic entity+free-text-constraint join (query_compilers.py compile_pubmed_call) does not reconstruct descriptive words from original_query that never appear as a structured entity or constraint value (e.g. FL-003's gold concepts include 'inhibitor' and 'resistance', neither of which is a ResearchQuery entity/constraint for that case) - this is an honestly measured, expected shortfall of a purely-structured-field compiler, not a bug.
parameter_quality.semantically_invalid_parameter_rate: NOT MEASURED - requires a semantic judge (LLM-as-judge or manual annotation), out of scope for a deterministic reproduction run; not fabricated.
parameter_quality.canonicalization_correctness_note: Covered by schema_valid_rate: ClinicalTrialsSearchArgs enforces VALID_TRIAL_STATUSES/VALID_TRIAL_PHASES at construction, and the compiler omits any raw value outside those sets before construction is even attempted - so no invalid status/phase can ever reach a counted call.

execution_safety_hard_gates.unregistered_tool_execution_note: 0 by construction: 0 call(s) across the run failed DEFAULT_REGISTRY.validate_call() (see registry_errors per case) and were never handed to get_execution_fn() - execution only ever runs over `validated_calls`. Additionally, the FL-003/FL-004 injected_tool_call fixtures were tested directly against the real ToolCall/ToolRegistry boundary (see hallucinated_tool_boundary_checks below) and both were rejected before execution.
execution_safety_hard_gates.arbitrary_model_generated_callable_execu: orchestration/registry.py statically binds execute_fn to the three real tool client methods at module import time - no eval/exec/dynamic import from any string anywhere in orchestration/ or query_compilers.py.
execution_safety_hard_gates.arbitrary_model_generated_url_execution_: All three tools use fixed hardcoded base URLs (tools/pubmed_tool.py, tools/clinical_trials_tool.py, tools/chembl_tool.py); query_compilers.py never constructs or passes a URL, only argument-schema fields.
execution_safety_hard_gates.secret_or_auth_header_in_trace_note: Regex-scanned every recorded call/arguments/error_summary field for api_key/authorization/bearer/secret substrings; all three tools are unauthenticated public GET APIs.
execution_safety_hard_gates.call_without_traceable_call_id_note: ToolCallBase.call_id (orchestration/models.py) is a required, non-empty field on every ToolCall subclass - pydantic construction itself would fail before a call could ever be compiled without one. 0 calls out of 67 were missing a call_id (should be 0).
execution_safety_hard_gates.unknown_tool_silent_fallback_note: Verified: every registry_errors entry is recorded as a rejected call, never substituted with a different tool and never executed.

execution_reliability.simulated_executions_note: 4 benchmark cases (FL-005 timeout, FL-006 rate_limit_429, FL-007 5xx, FL-008 empty_result) carry failure_injection.simulate_live_call=false in the manifest itself - per that explicit instruction, these calls were NOT executed live; a synthetic ToolExecutionResult was constructed instead (see execution_safety_hard_gates note and the per-case record for detail). Excluded from real success/failure/latency stats below.
execution_reliability.retry_count: NOT MEASURED DIRECTLY - retries happen transparently inside utils/retry_handler.py's RetrySession (same as Candidate A); observed in this run's logs (e.g. real PubMed 429s recovered automatically) but not persisted as a structured count by this harness.
execution_reliability.error_category_breakdown_note: Typed ToolErrorCategory values (orchestration/models.py) - for REAL (non-simulated) failures this is a string-matched heuristic over the real tool's free-text ToolResult.error (tools/base_tool.py handle_errors has no typed categories of its own), same honest-heuristic convention as the Candidate A baseline. For the 4 simulated cases the category is exact by construction (assigned directly, not inferred).
execution_reliability.known_preexisting_upstream_defect_note: 6 of the 6 real clinical_trials failures in this run are the SAME pre-existing defect in tools/clinical_trials_tool.py's search_trials() (lines ~247-256): whenever a valid 'phase' argument is supplied, the method emits a 'filter.phase=<value>' query parameter that clinicaltrials.gov's real v2 API rejects with HTTP 400 Bad Request (confirmed via the exact request URLs in the tool call history). This is NOT a Candidate C defect and NOT a schema-validation gap - the phase values Candidate C supplied (PHASE1/PHASE2/PHASE3/ EARLY_PHASE1) are all valid VALID_TRIAL_PHASES members and passed orchestration/models.py's ClinicalTrialsSearchArgs validation correctly. It is a pre-existing bug in the real tool client itself, independently reproduced: Candidate A's own baseline run (artifacts/v2/phase3_baseline_results.json) recorded the IDENTICAL 400 error with the identical 'filter.phase=...' query string for 5 of these 6 cases (CT-001, CT-003, CT-005, CT-011, CT-012) plus FL-002 - confirming this is a shared, upstream-tool-level defect affecting any candidate that supplies a phase filter, not something introduced or made worse by Candidate C's query compilers. Not fixed here (out of scope - tools/ is existing code and this task is additive-only); recorded honestly as a real execution_reliability failure, not concealed or reclassified.

multi_source.parallel_execution_success: N/A - this harness executes validated calls sequentially, one Python for-loop, matching Candidate A's own measurement scope (no asyncio/ThreadPoolExecutor path exists yet in orchestration/ either); no parallel path to measure for either candidate.

performance_latency_ms.source_selection_stage: NOT MEASURED SEPARATELY - orchestration.source_selection.select_sources() is a pure in-process function over an already-constructed ResearchQuery (no I/O, no model call); its wall-clock cost is sub-millisecond and not separately instrumented by this harness.
performance_latency_ms.query_compilation_stage: NOT MEASURED SEPARATELY - orchestration.query_compilers pure functions are in-process, no I/O, sub-millisecond; not separately instrumented.
performance_latency_ms.note: Simulated-failure-injection calls (4 of them, see execution_reliability) are excluded from all latency stats above since they made no real network call (latency_ms=0.0 by construction, not a real measurement).

cost.model_calls_per_case_note: 0 for every case, exactly, by construction - orchestration.source_selection.select_sources() and every function in orchestration/query_compilers.py are pure, deterministic Python (no LLM call anywhere in the Candidate C pipeline as measured here; see query_compilers.py module docstring for the PubMed-field determinism rationale).
cost.total_tokens_per_case: N/A - no LLM calls made, so no tokens consumed.
cost.dollar_cost_per_query: 0 (no LLM calls) plus unmeasured, unauthenticated public-API bandwidth cost - same NOT MEASURED reasoning as the Candidate A baseline for the latter (no pricing config exists for the free public APIs either, which is $0 by their own terms of use, not estimated).

traceability.valid_call_id_rate_note: Every ToolCall subclass requires a non-empty call_id at pydantic construction time (orchestration/models.py ToolCallBase.call_id) - structurally 1.0 for every call that exists in `calls` at all.
traceability.execution_result_linked_to_call_rate_not: ToolExecutionResult.call_id (orchestration/models.py) correlates 1:1 back to the ToolCall.call_id that produced it - this harness assigns execution_results[i].call_id = calls[i].call_id directly, never independently.
traceability.error_category_completeness_note: Fraction of non-success executions carrying a non-null typed ToolErrorCategory value. Real failures use the same string-matched heuristic as Candidate A (see execution_reliability note); simulated ones are exact by construction.
traceability.sanitized_trace_completeness_note: Regex-scanned (see execution_safety_hard_gates.secret_or_auth_header_in_trace_count) - all three tools are unauthenticated public GET APIs.
